text: Floating Clipboard Overlay (Visual Hijack) . category AI/ML Security . attack Clipboard Hijacking → Floating Overlay Exploit . text: NetBIOS Name Service (NBT-NS) Poisoning with Responder . category AI/ML Security . attack Internal Network Spoofing / Credential Harvesting . This simulation demonstrates how attackers use NBT-NS poisoning to capture NTLMv2 password hashes on local Windows networks. When a Windows machine fails to resolve a name via DNS, it sends out broadcast requests via NetBIOS-NS (UDP port 137). A malicious actor on the same network can respond to these requests, pretending to be the desired host. Once the victim connects, the attacker captures the authentication attempt (including password hash). This is a common tactic used in red teaming, internal pen tests, and post-exploitation lateral movement. target Enterprise LAN Internal Windows Workstations IoT devices with NetBIOS enabled . vulnerability - NetBIOS enabled on network - No hostname validation - NTLM fallback allowed

text: Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD) Abuse . category AI/ML Security . attack MLDv1/MLDv2 Flood / Multicast Discovery Exploit . This simulation demonstrates how attackers can exploit the IPv6 Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD) protocol to flood, crash, or overwhelm network devices. MLD is used by IPv6 hosts and routers to manage multicast group memberships, but it lacks authentication. An attacker can spoof fake MLD report or query messages using tools like mldq or flood_mld, causing excessive multicast state changes and traffic. On some systems (especially switches or routers), this can lead to resource exhaustion, denial of service, or even complete lock-up. This lab includes simulation of MLDv1/v2 flood attacks using Kali Linux and a Windows/Linux victim machine in a controlled test network. Ideal for labs, dataset collection, and switch stress testing. target WorkstationsSwitchesRoutersIoT DevicesCorporate VLAN users . vulnerability No authentication or rate-limiting in MLDUnmonitored multicast handling by switches and NICs
